bib.title: Linear Methods for Regression (Chapter 3 of The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed.)

question: How do least squares, subset selection, shrinkage (ridge, lasso, LAR) and derived-direction methods (PCR, PLS) fit linear regression models and trade bias for variance?

limits: The empirical comparison rests on one small dataset (97 cases, 67 train / 30 test), and test-error differences in Table 3.3 are within the printed standard errors (0.105 to 0.179).
Standard errors printed after a model search (Table 3.2 style) are not valid because they ignore the selection process; the bootstrap is suggested (Sec 3.3.2).
Stepwise selection by F-statistics is called out of fashion because it ignores multiple testing (Sec 3.3.2).
Ridge assumes the response varies most along high-variance input directions, which need not hold (Sec 3.4.1).
Lasso estimates of nonzero coefficients are biased toward zero and not consistent in general; relaxed lasso, SCAD and adaptive lasso are the cited fixes (Sec 3.8.5).
Dantzig selector has unsatisfactory operating properties and erratic paths (Sec 3.8.3).
Estimating q in the |beta|^q penalty from data is judged not worth the extra variance (Sec 3.4.3).
Backward stepwise needs N > p; best subset feasible only to p of about 30 or 40 (Sec 3.3).
Chapter text is 2009: later coordinate-descent (glmnet) and high-dimensional theory developments are not covered beyond Sec 3.8.6.
practices: Standardize inputs before ridge, lasso, PCR and PLS because they are not scale invariant (Sec 3.4.1, 3.5.1, 3.5.2).
Leave the intercept out of the ridge penalty and estimate it as the mean of y after centering inputs (Sec 3.4.1).
Choose the complexity parameter (subset size, lambda, t, M) by tenfold cross-validation on the training set only, keeping a test set to judge the chosen model (Sec 3.3.4).
Use the one-standard-error rule: pick the most parsimonious model within one standard error of the CV minimum (Sec 3.3.4).
Prefer forward stepwise over best subset when p is large or p exceeds N, since best subset costs variance and is infeasible (Sec 3.3.2).
Prefer ridge over PCR/PLS because it shrinks smoothly; use the lasso when sparse selection is wanted (Sec 3.6).
Use LAR with the lasso modification to compute the full lasso path at one least squares cost, or pathwise coordinate descent with warm starts over a lambda grid (Sec 3.4.4, 3.8.6).
Use the elastic net when predictors are correlated: selects like the lasso, shrinks correlated coefficients together (Sec 3.4.3).
Use grouped lasso when dummy variables or predefined groups should enter or leave together (Sec 3.8.4).
Use the QR decomposition (or Cholesky) rather than explicit inversion to fit least squares (Sec 3.2.3, 3.9).
Test groups of coefficients with the F statistic and not several single Z tests (Sec 3.2).
Fit multiple outputs separately by least squares; pooling (reduced-rank regression, curds and whey) helps only when responses share structure (Sec 3.2.4, 3.7).

terms.definition: The matrix H = X(X^T X)^-1 X^T that puts the hat on y; also a projection matrix.
Standardized coefficient z_j = beta_hat_j / (sigma_hat sqrt(v_j)), t-distributed with N-p-1 df under beta_j = 0, equivalent to the F statistic for dropping that coefficient.
df(y_hat) = (1/sigma^2) sum Cov(y_hat_i, y_i); for ridge equals tr[X(X^T X + lambda I)^-1 X^T] = sum d_j^2/(d_j^2+lambda).
Lasso estimate under orthonormal inputs: sign(beta_hat_j)(|beta_hat_j| - lambda)+.
Best-subset estimate under orthonormal inputs: beta_hat_j * I(|beta_hat_j| >= |beta_hat_(M)|).
Penalty lambda sum(alpha beta_j^2 + (1-alpha)|beta_j|), a compromise between ridge and lasso.

Forward-stepwise-like procedure that moves the coefficient of the predictor most correlated with the residual toward its least squares value until another predictor ties in correlation, then moves both along their joint least squares direction.
Repeatedly add epsilon * sign(<x_j, r>) to the coefficient of the predictor most correlated with the residual; the epsilon -> 0 limit is FS0.
Regress y on the first M principal component directions z_m = X v_m.
Build orthogonal directions z_m weighted by univariate effect of each x_j on y, orthogonalizing inputs after each; directions maximise Corr^2(y, X alpha) Var(X alpha).
Pick the most parsimonious model within one standard error of the minimum CV error.
Multivariate regression with rank(B) = m constraint; solution is a CCA of Y and X.
Penalty lambda sum sqrt(p_l) ||beta_l||_2 that shrinks and selects predefined groups together.
min ||beta||_1 subject to ||X^T (y - X beta)||_inf <= s, a linear program.

code.snippet: beta_ls = (X^T X)^-1 X^T y ;  beta_ridge = (X^T X + lambda I)^-1 X^T y
X = QR; beta_hat = R^-1 Q^T y; y_hat = Q Q^T y
X beta_ridge = sum_j u_j [d_j^2/(d_j^2+lambda)] u_j^T y ; df(lambda) = sum_j d_j^2/(d_j^2+lambda)
Best subset: b_j * I(|b_j| >= |b_(M)|); Ridge: b_j/(1+lambda); Lasso: sign(b_j)(|b_j| - lambda)+
z0 = x0 = 1; for j=1..p: regress x_j on z0..z_{j-1}, z_j = x_j - sum_k gamma_kj z_k; regress y on z_p to get beta_p

Standardize predictors (mean 0, unit norm); r = y - ybar; repeat: find x_j most correlated with r; move beta_j toward least squares coefficient until another competitor ties; then move tied set along joint LS direction delta = (X_A^T X_A)^-1 X_A^T r; after min(N-1,p) steps reach full LS. Lasso mod 3.2a: if a nonzero coefficient hits zero, drop it from the active set.
PLS: standardize x_j; for m=1..p: z_m = sum_j phi_mj x_j^(m-1), phi_mj = <x_j^(m-1), y>; theta_m = <z_m,y>/<z_m,z_m>; yhat^(m) = yhat^(m-1) + theta_m z_m; orthogonalize each x_j w.r.t. z_m
FS-eps: r = y, beta = 0, predictors standardized; repeat: j = argmax |<x_j, r>|; delta_j = eps * sign(<x_j, r>); beta_j += delta_j; r -= delta_j x_j
Coordinate descent lasso: beta_j <- S( sum_i x_ij (y_i - yhat_i^(j)), lambda ), S(t, lambda) = sign(t)(|t| - lambda)+; warm starts from lambda_max downward
